A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIPER work, and all supplied pages are readable. However, v1 includes Appendices A and B, while v2 ends with references and directs background, implementation details, and multi-frame SR comparisons to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF. This limits comparison of those materials.

before.justification: v1 Tables 1–4 report original FIPER super-resolution, compression, and ablation results. Appendix B also presents qualitative reconstruction results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and ablation results and adds single-image regression convergence and frequency-error measurements in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The factorized representation, sinusoidal modulation, sawtooth-aware downsampling, SR prior, and merged-basis compression procedure are retained. The corresponding proposed equations match across renumbering; v2's expanded component explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The documented training datasets, five SR benchmarks, three compression benchmarks, and single-image regression task are retained. v2 Section 4.1 additionally announces multi-frame SR comparisons exclusively in unavailable supplementary material, so the actual extension of evaluated task coverage cannot be verified.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds Plain Fields, a tensor-concatenation comparator, to single-image regression comparisons with FIPER and Chen et al.'s Factor Fields. The existing SR and compression comparator sets are unchanged; HAT-F-Concat already appeared in v1's separate SR comparison.

E3.justification: Figure 4 adds a diagnostic protocol tracking low- and high-frequency Fourier-magnitude error and PSNR through roughly 1,000 iterations. The existing training settings and 256-iteration representation ablation remain unchanged; the new trajectories do not establish a revised protocol for those retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 4 newly investigates convergence speed and fitting of different frequency components across three representations. Existing modulation, SR-prior, pipeline-order, and concatenation ablations remain. v1 Appendix B's additional qualitative examples are not included in the supplied v2.

E5.justification: Neither supplied version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability across runs for its original experiments. The new Figure 4 curves distinguish methods and frequency components, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the four existing tables are unchanged, including the ablation tables whose numbering is swapped. The compression rate-distortion curves are also retained. Figure 4 adds trajectories showing faster convergence, lower frequency error, and higher PSNR for FIPER; v1's additional appendix visual results are absent from v2.

T1.justification: The supplied v2 omits much of v1 Section 3.1's explicit mathematical background, including the channel-wise compression mapping in v1 Equation 4, and refers readers to unavailable supplementary material. The proposed factorization, SR, rate-distortion loss, and basis-merging equations are retained. This changes documented formal background without establishing a change to the underlying theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the unified representation, SR-prior integration, merged-basis compression, and state-of-the-art performance claims. The headline 204.4% relative SR improvement and 9.35% compression reduction claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning computation-limited applications such as real-time decoding and the absence of semantic modeling. It also interprets Figure 4 as evidence that modulation improves frequency alignment and convergence, expanding the explanation of the existing representation.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix A supplies architecture details such as a 384-dimensional Basis Swin Transformer, eight attention heads, and compression feature/stride settings that are not included in v2. The project-page link is also omitted. Common training hyperparameters remain, but v2's supplementary-material references do not supply the missing implementation information locally.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work coverage are retained. Both versions position FIPER as an extension of Factor Fields and a representation-focused contribution to SR and compression; the expanded explanation does not redefine that research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the preliminaries into supplementary-material references, expands the sawtooth and modulation explanations, and reverses the order of the two ablation discussions. Most abstract, introduction, related-work, and experimental prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from one column to two columns, with substantial resizing and relocation of figures and tables. v2 adds the decomposition illustration in Figure 1 and diagnostic plots in Figure 4, swaps Tables 3 and 4, and does not include v1's appendix architecture diagrams or additional visual-comparison grid.

improvement.justification: Figure 4, the expanded method explanation, and explicit limitations improve support and clarity. However, the supplied v2 loses self-contained mathematical and architectural documentation and additional visual evidence, while its claimed multi-frame comparisons remain unavailable. These benefits and documentation losses, together with the missing supplementary material, prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
